questions.prompt: What distinguishes an event from an appraisal?
questions.answer: An event is a circumstance; appraisal concerns its evaluated meaning or relevance.
questions.feedback: Separate the actual words from inferred intent.

questions.prompt: Does a genuine emotion establish that an interpretation is accurate?
questions.answer: No; the experience can be real while the external interpretation remains uncertain.
questions.feedback: Name evidence needed to test the interpretation.

questions.prompt: Why is the process model not a fixed one-way sequence?
questions.answer: Responses and changing situations can feed back into attention and appraisal.
When genuine danger or material constraints require safety action, support or structural change.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only. Use answer-specific feedback and delayed retest.
scoring.practice: Separates observed events, appraisals, responses and action tendencies; recognises feedback, uncertainty and safety constraints.
scoring.transfer: Write a novel fictional event–appraisal–response map with two plausible interpretations and a safety exception. Describe one possible feedback loop, such as how a response might change subsequent information.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; no averaging away omissions or safety-critical criteria. No automatic competency award.
